findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit the request context and are canceled after return
findings.body: The goroutine at this line wraps the incoming request context with a 10s timeout and then performs Legacy.Create. The same pattern is used for Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection (lines 108, 134, 161). In Kubernetes API server storage, the context passed to the storage method is typically canceled when the HTTP handler returns. Since this method returns immediately after launching the goroutine, the legacy backup write frequently starts with an already canceled context and is aborted, so mode 3 does not reliably keep legacy storage as a safe backup. Detach from the request lifecycle, for example with context.WithoutCancel/context.Background, before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Legacy update reuses the original UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the object written to unified storage
findings.body: This line passes the same `objInfo` that was already consumed by `d.Storage.Update` to `d.Legacy.Update`. `rest.UpdatedObjectInfo` may be single-use or may compute the new object against the old object in the target store; because legacy may have a different old object than unified storage, legacy can produce a different object or fail. The previous implementation wrapped the final object returned by storage in `updateWrapper` for the legacy update. The async legacy update should use the object returned by `d.Storage.Update`, or a wrapper that returns that object, rather than the original `objInfo`.

findings.title: Delete records the object name as the metric kind label
findings.body: This line passes `name` as the kind argument to `recordStorageDuration`, while other calls pass `options.Kind`. `name` is a user-controlled object name, so every deleted object creates a new Prometheus label value. This causes unbounded cardinality in the mode 3 storage metrics and can make metrics expensive or unusable. It should pass `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Storage create/update errors are recorded as legacy durations
findings.body: On a `Storage.Create` error, the code records `recordLegacyDuration` with the storage start time even though no legacy call was made. The same mistake is present in `Update` at line 129. These should be `recordStorageDuration`. As written, storage failure metrics are underreported and legacy duration metrics are polluted with storage call durations.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection result is recorded with the storage metric
findings.body: The async legacy `DeleteCollection` result is recorded with `recordStorageDuration` and `startLegacy`. It should use `recordLegacyDuration`. As written, legacy successes and failures are attributed to storage metrics, corrupting both metric sets.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests immediately assert legacy consistency despite async legacy writes
findings.body: The new mode 3 subtests run `doPlaylistTests`, which after k8s Create/Update immediately calls the legacy API and asserts that the change is present (for example the legacy list check and `getFromBothAPIs`). Mode 3 now writes to legacy asynchronously after the unified storage write returns, so these checks race with the legacy-write goroutine and can fail intermittently in CI. The tests should poll or wait for legacy convergence, or use a mode-specific expectation for async propagation.
